semmcci: Monte Carlo Confidence Intervals in Structural Equation Modeling

Source: R/semmcci-package.R
semmcci-package.Rd

Generates Monte Carlo confidence intervals for free and defined parameters in models fitted in the structural equation modeling package lavaan (Pesigan & Cheung, 2024). A sampling distribution of the parameter estimates is generated from the multivariate normal distribution using the parameter estimates and their sampling covariance matrix. Confidence limits are the percentiles of the generated distribution (Preacher & Selig, 2012; MacKinnon et al., 2004).

Models fitted in lavaan

MC() generates Monte Carlo confidence intervals from a fitted lavaan model. MCMI() does the same for a lavaan model fitted to multiply imputed data. MCStd() generates Monte Carlo confidence intervals for the standardized estimates from the output of MC() or MCMI().

Other models

MCGeneric() and MCFunc() generate Monte Carlo confidence intervals for functions of parameters when the estimates and their sampling covariance matrix are supplied. Func() does the same for a list of parameters.

Methods

The coef(), vcov(), confint(), summary(), and print() methods are available for objects of class semmcci.

References

MacKinnon, D. P., Lockwood, C. M., & Williams, J. (2004). Confidence limits for the indirect effect: Distribution of the product and resampling methods. Multivariate Behavioral Research, 39(1), 99–128. doi:10.1207/s15327906mbr3901_4

Pesigan, I. J. A., & Cheung, S. F. (2024). Monte Carlo confidence intervals for the indirect effect with missing data. Behavior Research Methods. doi:10.3758/s13428-023-02114-4

Preacher, K. J., & Selig, J. P. (2012). Advantages of Monte Carlo confidence intervals for indirect effects. Communication Methods and Measures, 6(2), 77–98. doi:10.1080/19312458.2012.679848
